top_cited_works.title: Surrogate-based aerodynamic shape optimization for delaying airfoil dynamic stall using Kriging regression and infill criteria
Surrogate-Based Aerodynamic Shape Optimization by Variable-Resolution Models
top_cited_works.abstract: A surrogate-based optimization algorithm for transonic airfoil design is presented. The approach replaces the direct optimization of an accurate, but computationally expensive, high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics model by an iterative reoptimization of a physics-based surrogate model. The surrogate model is constructed, during each design iteration, using the low-fidelity model and the data obtained from one high-fidelity model evaluation. The low-fidelity model is based on the same governing fluid flow equations as the high-fidelity one, but uses coarser mesh resolution and relaxed convergence criteria. The shape-preserving response prediction technique is utilized to predict the high-fidelity model response, here, the airfoil pressure distribution. In this prediction process, the shape-preserving response prediction employs the actual changes of the low-fidelity model response due to the design variable adjustments. The shape-preserving response prediction algorithm is embedded into the trust region framework that ensures good convergence properties of the optimization procedure. recent_works.title: Adaptive Hyperparameter Optimization Strategies for Neural Network Models in Engineering Design Optimization
recent_works.abstract: Surrogate-based optimization using neural networks (NNs) reduces computational costs in engineering design but depends heavily on systematic hyperparameter optimization (HPO). This study compares HPO methods—including grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization (BO), hyperband (HB), and BOHB—using analytical functions and aerodynamic shape optimization (ASO). The study first explores HPO in a one-shot method where NNs are trained with datasets of different sample sizes. The analysis then extends to adaptive HPO approaches within an efficient global optimization (EGO) framework using NNs, which employs sequential sampling. Under this framework, static HPO (maintaining initially optimized HPs), periodic HPO (adjusting HPs every five infill points), and dynamic HPO (adjusting HPs after each infill point) are compared. recent_works.title: Special Issue: Data-Driven Design Under Uncertainty
recent_works.abstract: Advances in data acquisition, high-performance computing, and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the way engineers conceive, analyze, and optimize complex mechanical systems. Across applications as diverse as materials discovery, manufacturing process optimization, digital twins, robotics, and resilient network design, the engineering community increasingly relies on data-driven methods to model systems characterized by high dimensionality, evolving states, and heterogeneous sources of uncertainty. As these systems grow in complexity, uncertainty quantification (UQ) and design under uncertainty have become foundational to ensuring that engineered solutions are robust, reliable, and trustworthy. This special issue of the ASME Journal of Mechanical Design was conceived to bring together fundamental contributions that expand the capabilities of UQ and uncertainty-aware design optimization in the age of modern ML. The call emphasized interpretability, scalability, multi-fidelity reasoning, and the integration of new paradigms—including generative AI, probabilistic deep learning, graph-based representations, and large language models—into engineering workflows. recent_works.title: Efficient Design of Airfoil Shapes Using Surface Pressure–Informed Bayesian Optimization
recent_works.abstract: Aerodynamic shape optimization (ASO) of airfoil shapes is an essential part of the aerodynamic design process. Optimizing the shape of an airfoil is a challenging and time-consuming task when computationally expensive numerical simulations are required. As an alternative, surrogate-based optimization methods, such as machine learning models and Bayesian optimization (BO), have been explored to optimize the shapes of airfoils. However, most currently used methods do not utilize information from surface pressure distributions in creating the surrogate model or the optimization search. Surface pressure distributions are essential aerodynamic features that influence the design of an airfoil. As such, this work proposes surface pressure-informed Bayesian optimization (SPINBO), a novel BO methodology that incorporates surface pressure distribution information into the surrogate modeling methodology and relates the pressure distribution to the aerodynamic coefficients. The proposed approach is characterized using the drag minimization problem of the RAE 2822 airfoil in transonic viscous flow at a Mach number of 0.734 and a Reynolds number of 6.5 million. recent_works.title: Aerodynamic Uncertainty Analysis of the Common Research Model Wing Using Autoencoders
recent_works.abstract: Uncertainties in the operations and design of aircraft wings are unavoidable, making it necessary to analyze uncertainties in both surface pressure distributions and aerodynamic coefficients to ensure robustness and reliability in wing design. However, uncertainty analysis through Monte Carlo simulations is prohibitive due to the computational expense of numerical simulations required to evaluate a wing design. Surrogate models can be used to alleviate the expense, but current models typically do not offer predictions of both surface pressure distributions and aerodynamic coefficients for highly nonlinear flow regimes to analyze uncertainties in both simultaneously. As such, this paper proposes UQAeroNet, a neural network architecture that can simultaneously provide a prediction of the surface pressure distribution and the aerodynamic coefficients for the uncertainty analysis of both types of quantities. The proposed approach is characterized by using the NASA Common Research Model wing in transonic viscous flow at a Mach number of 0.80 and Reynolds number of 5.18 million. recent_works.title: Efficient Design Under Uncertainty of Spacecraft and Trajectory Systems Using Gaussian Process Surrogates
recent_works.abstract: Design under uncertainty for coupled spacecraft propulsion and interplanetary trajectory systems is prohibitive due to the large number of high-fidelity multidisciplinary analysis (MDA) evaluations required for Monte Carlo-based reliability assessment. This paper presents a surrogate-enabled design under uncertainty framework for a coupled spacecraft and trajectory Earth--Mars transfer problem inspired by MAVEN, using both reliability-based design optimization (RBDO) and robust design optimization (RDO). The high-fidelity MDA integrates the Rocket Propulsion Analysis (RPA) tool and NASA’s General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT) within OpenMDAO to model a single-stage chemical propulsion spacecraft executing a trajectory correction maneuver (TCM) and Mars orbit insertion (MOI). Gaussian process (GP) surrogates, trained on MDA-generated samples and used with Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), provide low-cost predictions of time of flight and burn-wise fuel consumption.
